Metabase is the easiest way for people to get insights from their data, from tiny startups who get up and running quickly to major corporations with tens of thousands of users. That's why people love us.
We bring data tools with the elegance and simplicity of consumer products to the crufty world of enterprise business intelligence. We provide an opinionated open source starting point for how companies should measure, analyze and share their data, which is used by tens of thousands of companies.
We built Metabase because existing tools for business intelligence didn’t feel like things we wanted to use. We wanted faster, simpler ways to ask questions about data, and wanted to strip away the colder feel of most Enterprise software. Folks seemed to agree, and now Metabase is used daily by tens of thousands of companies to give people in all sorts of roles access to insights they wouldn’t have otherwise had. None of this could happen without our user interface and that’s where you come in. We’re looking for someone with strong product sensibilities, extraordinarily good frontend skills, and solid software engineering fundamentals to join our team to advance the state of the art in our product and our industry.
We are hiring for multiple frontend software engineer positions.

• The problems we face are genuinely interesting and aren’t trivial. Data influences so much of our world but isn’t that easy to interact with or understand. You’ll make tools that people rely on for their real jobs.

• You’ll get to work in open source and get feedback directly from users and customers out in the open.

• The company is growing and so is the business. We’re adding new remote team members from around the world and improving our processes. It’s an exciting time and you can really have an impact on how things work here.

• We’ve tried to design our work environment to fit into real life. Work is only one part of who you are, so we emphasize reasonable workdays and prefer planning and avoiding panic. People at Metabase have families, dogs, plants, and lives outside of work and we try to support that however we can.

What we're looking for

•
You care about crafting delightful user experiences . You like to write code to enable people to do something and you understand that details and things like copy matter. If your focus is only on code this might not be the best role for you.

•
Prior experience shipping non-trivial apps using React + Redux (or equivalent) . Our front end is written in React (surprise!), so you’ll need really strong React and JavaScript knowledge to build fast and thoughtful user interfaces.

• You have experience writing tests, giving good feedback on other people’s code , and writing proposals for more complicated problems that are thoughtful and clear. As we’re a remote company (even outside of pandemics) communication and clarity are really important .

• You’ve worked on a large and complex JavaScript project. Metabase is a big product and code base so the ability to adapt existing code and integrate new code into established systems is important and you should feel comfortable digging in.

ClickHouse has a lot worth saying. The database has become a platform for real-time analytics, data warehousing, observability, and AI workloads. Many of the most interesting AI and software companies of the last few years run on it. Our founders and leaders hold clear, well-formed views on where data and AI are heading. And every week the customer base produces proof points most companies would build a campaign around. What we have not yet built is the function whose job it is to turn all of that into one story the market hears consistently, and from us.

We are looking for a Senior Director, Story & Communications to build that function from the ground up. You'll own the company narrative: what ClickHouse should be known for, how the platform story gets told above the level of features, and how the proof we generate adds up to a thesis. And you'll build the machine that carries it into the world: the announcement calendar, press and media relationships across technology and business media, and executive platforms for our founders and leaders. This is a build role and a player-coach role. You won't inherit a team; you'll hire one as the function grows, directing our agency partners in the meantime and staying in the work yourself. You'll report to the VP of Global Marketing and work closely with the executive team, product marketing, and the people closest to our customers.

What You Will Be Doing

- Define what ClickHouse should be known for and turn it into a rolling narrative and communications strategy that the marketing and executive teams work from

- Build the communications machine: announcement calendar and tiering, press materials, holding statements, a reporter cadence, and launch amplification, directing agency partners and holding them to outcomes

- Own press and media relations across technology and business media, taking the ClickHouse story beyond the tech press and re-educating the market on the full platform

- Build executive platforms for our founders and leaders: the themes each owns, the moments and formats worth their time, and a clear way to evaluate inbound podcast, mainstage, and sponsored event opportunities

- Shape quarterly release moments and major launches so they earn attention and show up consistently across press, social, community, and the field

- Set the standard for how ClickHouse sounds in public: voice, quality bar, and the discipline that every published claim, number, and proof point is approved, current, and consistent

- Hire and lead the team as the function grows, and build the planning and review rhythm that keeps narrative, communications, and social aligned

What You Bring Along

- Experience building or rebuilding a communications function at a growth-stage infrastructure, developer, or data company

- A record of landing stories in tier-one business media as well as technology press, with the relationships and news judgment to do it again

- Experience working directly with a CEO and executive team: shaping their points of view, preparing them, and declining opportunities not worth their time

- Media-company operator instincts: you think in themes, arcs, and audiences

- Player-coach approach: you write and edit yourself, give useful feedback, and set the bar by example

- Comfort with a technical product and a technical audience, including credibility with engineers and developers

- Experience directing agencies to outcomes, with judgment about what belongs in-house

- Analytical grounding: you track what is landing, form a view on why, and use it to decide where to focus

PERKS

- Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

- Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

- Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

- Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

Team members have the opportunity to see their work make a meaningful difference in real pharmacies while contributing to technology that helps healthcare professionals focus on what matters most: their patients.
